claim: When the cost of performing self-repair is accounted for, performance gains are often modest, vary widely across data subsets, and are sometimes entirely absent, across Code Llama, GPT-3.5, and GPT-4 on HumanEval and APPS.
stance_target: self-repair as a reliably strong inference-time method
scope_conditions: Code Llama, GPT-3.5, GPT-4; HumanEval and APPS; ICLR 2024
quoted_support: We find that when the cost of carrying out repair is taken into account, performance gains are often modest, vary a lot between subsets of the data, and are sometimes not present at all.

claim: Self-repair is bottlenecked by the model's own ability to generate useful feedback on its own code; artificially boosting feedback quality with a stronger model yields substantially larger performance gains.
stance_target: hypothesis that feedback-signal quality, not repair mechanics, is the binding constraint on self-repair
quoted_support: We hypothesize that this is because self-repair is bottlenecked by the model's ability to provide feedback on its own code; using a stronger model to artificially boost the quality of the feedback, we observe substantially larger performance gains.

claim: Even the strongest model tested (GPT-4) self-repairs far worse than when given human-level debugging feedback.
quoted_support: a small-scale study in which we provide GPT-4 with feedback from human participants suggests that even for the strongest models, self-repair still lags far behind what can be achieved with human-level debugging.
